evidence.title: Brand in BP-Raffinerie Scholven unter Kontrolle: keine Gefahr für Bevölkerung (Dorsten Online, 15 Jul 2026; BP statement)
evidence.excerpt: Fire around 17:00 on 15 July 2026 in a diesel desulphurisation unit (Diesel-Entschwefelungsanlage) at BP's Scholven site, brought under control the same evening by the works fire brigade with Gelsenkirchen, Marl and Marl chemical park fire services. No injuries; no danger to public health per BP; odour may persist; cause unclear. Initial reports: a pipeline carrying sulphur-containing gas was affected, isolated on both sides and allowed to burn out under control.
evidence.note: site, unit, duration of fire, casualties

evidence.title: Brand bei BP in Gelsenkirchen-Scholven: Nina warnt (Radio Vest, 16 Jul 2026 10:11)
evidence.excerpt: The Recklinghausen district control centre issued a precautionary NINA/Katwarn warning for Marl, Gladbeck, Dorsten and Herten for possible odour nuisance and smoke deposits; residents told to stay indoors, keep windows and doors closed and switch off ventilation; no protective measures beyond that were required. Smoke plume visible across the Recklinghausen district.

evidence.url: search:argus gelsenkirchen fire diesel desulphurisation unit loadings halted 13 july pipeline maintenance
evidence.title: Argus market coverage of the fire (quoted in search results; article URL not retained)
evidence.excerpt: A fire at BP's 251,000 b/d Gelsenkirchen refinery shut a diesel desulphurisation unit; BP said the rest of the plant was unaffected. Local traders said diesel and gasoline loadings at the refinery had already been halted since 13 July for pipeline maintenance, so the unit outage initially had no additional market effect. Separately, German heating oil and diesel prices rose by up to EUR 11.40/100l on 14 July after the US announced a resumed blockade on Iranian vessels in Hormuz; futures...
evidence.note: fuel-market trace: none attributable; loadings already stopped; macro tide from Hormuz

evidence.title: Fire at German BP refinery; INEOS declares force majeure on phenol and acetone and implements sales allocation (ChemNet, 29 Jul 2026)
evidence.excerpt: The fire prompted BP to fully suspend all benzene deliveries. Benzene from BP goes to INEOS's cumene plant in Marl and the cumene to Gladbeck (650 kt/y phenol, 400 kt/y acetone). INEOS Phenol declared force majeure on European phenol and acetone and rolled out a sales quota allocation cutting deliveries to all customers proportionally. As of 27 July 2026 the force majeure and quota remain in effect; no timeline for normal deliveries, restart tied to the repair and commissioning schedule of...
evidence.note: petrochemical offtake carrier: force majeure within 14 days; the fire was in a fuels unit yet site-wide deliveries stopped

evidence.title: Klesch becomes Germany's second-largest oil refiner after BP deal (Yahoo/Investing.com, 8 Aug 2026)
evidence.excerpt: Klesch Group completed the acquisition of BP's Gelsenkirchen refinery business (roughly 265,000 b/d). Only mention of the incident: a fire at Gelsenkirchen in July temporarily shut several units, including one used to produce diesel. No effect of the fire on the deal is reported.
evidence.note: several units shut, described as temporary by 8 Aug; sale completed on the pre-announced timetable

evidence.title: bp agrees to sell 12-MMtpy Gelsenkirchen refinery to Klesch Group (Hydrocarbon Processing, Mar 2026); completion release bp.com 3 Aug 2026
evidence.excerpt: BP agreed in March 2026 to sell the Gelsenkirchen business (12 Mt/y, ~1,800 employees) to Klesch Group, closing expected in H2 2026 subject to approvals. BP's German press release of 3 August 2026 announces completion of the sale; BP's 2Q26 results on 4 August reflect the completed sale. No source cites the 15 July fire as changing the timetable or terms.
evidence.note: sale timetable before and after the event

evidence.title: Investment update on BP, 14 Jul 2026 (Patronus Partners) and Hormuz context
evidence.excerpt: Brent climbed to USD 85 on 14 July, up more than 10% on the week, after the US reinstated a blockade on Iranian vessels transiting Hormuz. BP's trading statement ahead of 4 August results pointed to strong oil prices and refining margins. No source attributes any BP share move on 15 to 17 July to the Gelsenkirchen fire.
evidence.note: owner equity sat inside a macro tide; no attributed move found

resolutions.scorer_note: First clean round; self-scored, human to ratify. Map: BP-owned Scholven site under an agreed sale (Klesch) right; contained same evening, no injuries right. Sub-claim that the main chemical offtaker is the co-located polyolefin producer was off: the offtaker that mattered was the INEOS benzene-cumene-phenol chain. Falsifier did not fire. Quarantined by choice: the cited rule did not carry a map claim; no mechanism rode this call.

Sources conflict on scope (Argus/BP: one unit, rest unaffected; ChemNet: full production halt; Yahoo 8 Aug: several units temporarily shut). No restart date for the unit or for benzene deliveries found; force majeure still in effect on 27 July, described as temporary by 8 Aug. Neither the claim (back within 6 weeks, by 26 Aug) nor the falsifier (still out on 1 Sep) can be established. Coverage thin: trade press paywalled, BP pages unreachable.

No attributable step: Argus reports no additional market effect. But the stated reason was that loadings had been halted since 13 July for pipeline maintenance, with prices driven by the Hormuz blockade, not the slack mechanism the call rode. Right call, wrong relation: quarantined. Baseline (fuel prices up on a refinery fire) wrong as to attribution.

The fire was in a fuels unit, yet BP suspended all benzene deliveries and INEOS Phenol declared force majeure on phenol and acetone with allocation, within the 14-day window (in effect by 27 July). The call's second branch ('if only the fuels side burned, no notice') fired the falsifier. The mechanism was right (force majeure was the fast public carrier, as in round 2); the conditional was a misread: a fire anywhere on an integrated site stops the site's deliveries.

Ordering held: physical (several units shut) > offtake (benzene suspended; phenol/acetone force majeure and allocation, 15 rail cars cut to 10, still in force 12 days later) > regional fuel differentials (nil, loadings already stopped) > equity (nil). Baseline (everything moves on the day) wrong.

Null hit, weight 0.2. No listed party's move in the three sessions after 15 July was attributed to the fire; BP sat inside the Hormuz oil tide (Brent +10% on the week). Baseline (owner down): direction unverifiable against the tide.

Null hit, weight 0.2. At event time the owner was a supermajor with the site already agreed for sale, the buyer and the affected offtaker are private, and every holder on the node is sign minus. Falsifier window scoring_window (to 12 Aug): no listed concentrated holder emerged. Baseline (trade the disruption): unverified.
The sale to Klesch completed on 3 August 2026 on the pre-announced H2 timetable; no source cites the fire as changing terms or timing. No-mechanism call by declaration.

NINA/Katwarn warning issued on the day for four towns; no regulator order constraining the site found within 14 days (German and English searched). Quarantined: the cited inspection-order rule concerns fatal accidents and did not operate here (no injuries); liability_periphery did not ride either.
